kicker: A garden with a gate — who holds the key? In other words: who decides how you get to use AI.
summary: Who may use a model, whose data it learned from, and what you must label: companies, courts and each country’s laws are deciding together.

options: Everything is public, even the data used to teach the model
Download what the model learned, run it, teach it more
Anyone can change the model right on its maker's own servers
You may use it however you like, with no licence to follow
quiz.explain: Open weights means you can download the “brain” it learned. The data used to teach it usually is not included, and the licence still says how you may use it.

gate.label: Walled garden, open garden
gate.art: A black lacquer tray stands in the water under the moon; on it, a round moss island split in two. One half is a garden behind a whitewashed wall, with only a lit window handing out sprigs of blossom: you use the model only through the company's app. The other half is a garden with its bamboo gate wide open, a sapling in a pot you can carry away, stepping stones across the water to houses on the far shore: you download the model to your own machine. Four stone lanterns round the rim, each a gain and a loss.
gate.closed: Walled garden · closed model (used only through the company's app)
gate.open: Open garden · open model (you can download it)
gate.toggleAria: Switch between the walled garden and the open garden
gate.tradeoffLabel: What you gain, what you give up

tradeoffs.name: Freedom
tradeoffs.closed: You play by the company's rules; you cannot change the inside.
tradeoffs.open: Download it, teach it more, run it wherever you like.

tradeoffs.name: Cost
tradeoffs.closed: Pay per use or by plan; no powerful computer needed.
tradeoffs.open: No per-use fees, but you supply the hardware, power and upkeep.

tradeoffs.name: Privacy
tradeoffs.closed: Your data passes through the company's servers.
tradeoffs.open: Run it on your own machine and your data never leaves it.

tradeoffs.name: Risk of misuse
tradeoffs.closed: The company can block harmful requests and close abusive accounts.
tradeoffs.open: Once released it cannot be recalled; others can strip out its safety guards.

insight.text: The walled garden only hands a sprig through the window: you use the model through the company's app. The open garden lets you take the tree home: you download the model.

detail.text: “Open weights” means the company lets you download the part of the model that has learned. For example, in Aug 2025 OpenAI released gpt-oss, usable even for business (Apache 2.0 licence); the small version runs on a 16 GB machine.

gate.caveat: The data the model learned from usually stays secret. Where to download models: station 31.
prompts: Drag sideways to turn the tray and see the other garden
Light the lanterns to compare the two gardens

fence.label: Fenced-off models
fence.art: Night, seen low at ground level: a cold white lamp, the model, inside a fence of bamboo stakes bound with thorny rope; each stake throws a long shadow fanning toward the viewer. Behind, a long castle wall, the software, recedes into the mist; where the beam touches it, cracks with vermilion lips show: security flaws. Two guards holding stamped paper lanterns stand at the gate.
fence.gateAria: Try the fence gate: see who gets in and why
fence.lampAria: Turn the lamp (the model) across the wall (the software): left and right arrows
fence.denied: The gate opens only for vetted people who fix software flaws.

fact.text: Apr 2026: Anthropic gave Mythos Preview only to organisations that find and fix software flaws, with no plan for a wide release.
Sep 2026: Google set up its Fairwind programme, giving its strongest cybersecurity model only to vetted people who fix flaws.

why.text: This model finds software flaws better than most experts (Anthropic says so itself). Hand it out widely and attackers could use it too.

debate.text: Who chooses who gets inside the fence, and who checks what the company says about its own model?

insight.text: The lamp is the model, the cracks are software flaws. It finds them too well, so the company hands the lamp only to vetted flaw-fixers.

detail.text: In 2026 Anthropic (Mythos Preview) and Google (Fairwind) both did this.

prompts: Turn the lamp to search the wall

laws.label: The tide of law
laws.art: From the sea at night, looking at the shore: four equal stone pillars stand in a row, their names carved above them: EU, China, US, Vietnam; at first their feet are under the waves. Drag the moon along the dotted ink arc in the sky (marked 2024, 2025, 2026, Today): the tide draws back toward you, and when a place's law takes effect its pillar shows one more notch, the words carved right under its foot. The EU's high-risk notch slides down to its new deadline; the US pillar cracks down the middle; China's and Vietnam's carry a label seal; Vietnam's is still wet.
laws.prompt: Drag the moon through the years and watch each place's laws rise
laws.sliderAria: Drag the moon through the years to see each place's AI-law milestones
notches: Vietnam · Dec 2025 has an AI law
US · Dec 2025 federal government takes on state laws
Vietnam · May 2026 AI content must be marked
EU · high-risk AI pushed to Dec 2027

milestones.label: EU: the AI Act takes effect

fact.text: The EU AI Act takes effect, phased in by the risk level of each kind of application; AI used to hire people or decide on loans, for example, counts as high-risk.
EU bans start to apply to AI uses with unacceptable risk, such as scoring citizens on their behaviour.
China requires AI-generated content to be labelled: a visible label and a hidden one in the file's data.
The National Assembly passes the Artificial Intelligence Law: 35 articles, risk-based rules, in force from 1 March 2026.

milestones.label: US: an order on state laws

fact.text: Dec 2025: the US President set up a federal legal task force to challenge state AI laws he considers a burden on business.
Decree 142/2026 takes effect: AI is split into three risk levels, and AI-made images, audio and video must carry an identifying mark.
The EU amends the law (an amending package called the Omnibus): high-risk AI rules move to 2 Dec 2027, and AI built into products to 2 Aug 2028.

horizon.text: AI law will keep being rewritten as the technology changes; today's deadline may not be tomorrow's.

insight.text: The EU sorts AI by risk, China and Vietnam require labels, and the US is still torn between federal and state.

detail.text: According to an analysis by the law firm Tilleke & Gibbins (June 2026), Vietnam's list of high-risk AI systems was still waiting for the Prime Minister to issue it.

board.text: Making content in Vietnam: AI-made images, audio and video must carry an identifying mark (Decree 142/2026).

copyright.label: Whose data teaches AI
copyright.art: At the edge of a moonlit pond: a well-sweep crosses the frame on a diagonal, its bucket hanging from the pole over the water. The pond reflects not the sky but a whole library: pages, scrolls and sheet music drifting underwater like fish, the data used to teach AI. Four big stones stand on the near bank, each seeing the bucket of data in its own way.
copyright.sweepAria: Pull the well-sweep: dip the bucket into the lake and lift it

view.text: Oct 2024: tens of thousands of artists and writers signed a statement: taking work without permission to teach AI is unjust.
OpenAI (Jan 2024): teaching AI on public material online is “fair use”, meaning it can be used without asking under US law; anyone who objects can ask to opt out.
June 2025, a US judge: teaching AI with lawfully bought books is fair use; downloading pirated books to build a library is not.
The EU requires companies making models for many uses to respect copyright and publish a summary of the data they used.

common.text: The data in the bucket has value. Still unsettled: how far AI must ask permission from, and pay, the people who made it.

cases.text: Jul 2026: Anthropic pays $1.5 billion, about $3,000 a book, to authors whose books were pirated to teach AI.

insight.text: Sep 2026: a US appeals court ruled that Ross, a legal-AI company, was not allowed to copy Westlaw's legal notes to teach its AI.

prompts: Drag the sweep to lift data out of the pond
Touch each stone: everyone sees the bucket differently
